content.title: About
content.content: Freezer pop is a frozen dessert pop – a flavored ice lollipop on a stick. It is made from water, sugar, fruit or berry concentrates and sometimes a small amount of dairy. The product is popular as a refreshing treat in hot weather.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Freezer pop originated in the United States in the 1960s and quickly became a summer favorite.
It often contains natural fruit extracts, giving it a bright and intense flavor.
The stick format makes it easy to eat on the go.
There are many flavor variations: strawberry, lemon, watermelon, mango, and more.
Freezer pop is frequently used in culinary shows to create “icy” visual effects.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content helps maintain fluid balance, especially in warm conditions.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Unlike traditional ice cream, frozen pops contain virtually no fat.

items.title: Source of Vitamin C
items.content: Fruit concentrates can provide a modest amount of vitamin C, supporting immunity.

items.title: Moderate Sugar Levels
items.content: Sugar content is generally lower than in non‑frozen candies, making it a less calorie‑dense snack.

items.title: Easy Digestion
items.content: The frozen form melts slowly, which can be gentler on the digestive system.

items.title: Allergy to Fruit Ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the fruit extracts used.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Despite being moderate, the product still contains sugar and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Risk of Frostbite
items.content: Prolonged contact with the frozen pop may cause mild frostbite of the oral mucosa.

items.title: Not Suitable for Young Children
items.content: Because of the stick and solid form, there is a choking hazard for small children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Freezer pop is typically served frozen, held by the stick, and allowed to melt slowly in the mouth. It can be stored in the freezer for up to 6 months. It can also be added to drinks or used as a garnish for desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep Freezer pop in an airtight container in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Avoid prolonged exposure at room temperature to prevent melting and loss of texture.
